scenarios.description: Matching segmented-RAG trace with a genuine cross-boundary support dependency: an exemption clause needed to correctly qualify the answer is retrieved and selected but not packed.
scenarios.notes: The clean positive case: a real, material dependency crosses the boundary and never reaches the generator.

scenarios.description: Segmented-RAG trace with a single self-contained supporting segment and no cross-boundary dependency at all.
scenarios.notes: Clean negative case: chunking exists, but there is no dependency to split. Must not activate merely because chunking is present.

scenarios.description: Whole-document retrieval (no sub-document segmentation exists) -- the mechanism is structurally inapplicable even though the trace deliberately (and incorrectly) carries a boundary-dependency flag.
scenarios.notes: Disqualifying manifest gate (retrieval_unit=whole_document) takes precedence over any trace content.

scenarios.description: chunking_method and retrieval_unit are both unknown in the manifest; the mechanism must report insufficient information rather than assume either way.
scenarios.notes: Gate outcome is unknown_insufficient_data, distinct from both activation and clean disqualification.

scenarios.description: A support relation crosses a segment boundary, but both segments were retrieved, selected, and packed together -- full support reached the generator despite the boundary crossing.
scenarios.notes: Deliberately ambiguous: the trace-level trigger fires (a boundary was crossed) but the outcome is benign -- informative for false-reassurance and unnecessary-escalation analysis, since the mechanism does not itself assess completeness beyond the flag's presence.

scenarios.description: A support relation crosses a segment boundary and the dependent segment is explicitly omitted before generation (context_budget_exceeded).
scenarios.notes: Fullest-detail positive case, with an explicit omission_reason -- the clearest scenario for measuring whether the warning helps reviewers notice a traceable, material omission.

scenarios.description: A support relation crosses a segment boundary and the dependent segment is omitted, but a different, complete, self-contained source independently supports the same answer and was packed.
scenarios.notes: Redundant-support case: the mechanism fires (a real omission occurred) but the answer remains supported via an independent source -- tests whether the warning leads to unnecessary rejection.

scenarios.description: The query omits the weight-class and region parameters that determine the answer; the system answered with an assumption instead of asking.
scenarios.notes: No defensible single gold label exists until the missing parameters are known -- adjudication_applicable is False by design, not a gap. Illustrates user-intent responsiveness independent of the segmentation mechanism.

scenarios.description: Two versions of the handbook give different processing times; the answer silently picked one without surfacing the conflict.
scenarios.notes: Distinct mechanism (GEN_CONTEXT_CONFLICT_UNRESOLVED-adjacent), included to give the reviewer-study material where 'unresolved'/'version_dependent' is the correct outcome, not a factual miss.

scenarios.description: A required-support-item split is flagged, but the split-off segment is a page-footer formatting note with no bearing on the answer.
scenarios.notes: The mechanism fires on an immaterial split -- a case for measuring unnecessary_escalation_count and whether reviewers correctly recognize low materiality rather than escalating by default.

scenarios.description: A safety-relevant carve-out (lithium sub-assembly exception) is split across a segment boundary and omitted before generation; under manifest_conditioned the resulting risk event's priority is capped below HIGH regardless of this case's real materiality.
scenarios.notes: Structurally identical to case 06 but framed to probe false reassurance specifically: does a capped-priority warning still get the scrutiny this genuinely material omission deserves?
